questions.question: A paperclip is about 3 __.
questions.explain: A paperclip is small, so we use centimetres. Metres and kilometres are for much bigger things.

questions.question: 1 kilometre is the same as ___ metres.
questions.explain: 1 kilometre = 1000 metres. The trap is using 100, which is the step from metres to centimetres.

questions.question: The distance between two small towns is about 4 __.
questions.explain: Towns are far apart, so kilometres fit. Centimetres and metres are too small for a town-to-town trip.

questions.question: A desk is about 70 __ wide.
questions.explain: A desk is small enough to measure in centimetres. 70 metres would be as long as a big swimming pool!

questions.question: Mia measures her bed. It is 200 centimetres long. In metres, that is ___.
questions.explain: 200 cm = 2 m because 100 cm = 1 m. Be careful not to just copy the number 200.

questions.question: Your school is 800 metres away. That is about ___ kilometres.
questions.explain: 800 m is just under 1 km (1000 m). Dividing by 100 gives 8, but you should divide by 1000.

questions.question: A door in your house is about __ tall.
questions.explain: A door is about 2 metres tall. 2 cm is as small as a coin, and 2 km is a very long walk.

questions.question: A road sign says 'Next town: 1 km.' A car drives 800 m. Has it reached the town yet?
options: Yes, 800 m is more than 1 km
No, 800 m is less than 1 km
questions.explain: 800 m is less than 1000 m (1 km), so the car has not reached the town yet. 1 km is 1000 m, not 100 m.

questions.question: A rope is 3 metres long. A stick is 250 centimetres long. Which is longer?
questions.explain: 3 m = 300 cm, and 300 cm is more than 250 cm, so the rope is longer. Change to the same unit before comparing.

questions.question: Two friends each walk 500 metres to the park. Together they walked ___.
questions.explain: 500 m + 500 m = 1000 m, which is 1 km. A common mistake is dividing by 100 and getting 10 km.

questions.question: Ava tells her cousin about the big cedar tree at her park. The tree is much taller than her house. Which height fits the tree best?
questions.explain: A tree taller than a house is about 20 metres. Centimetres are for small things like a crayon, and kilometres are for long trips.

questions.question: Emma wants to know how far it is around her school running track. She looks in the gym shed for a tool. Which tool and unit fit best?
questions.explain: A track is a few hundred metres, so a metre stick and metres fit well. Kilometres are for long trips, like a drive to another town.

questions.question: Priya makes a list of things to measure on her class trip. Only one of them is best measured in kilometres. Which one is it?
questions.explain: Kilometres are for long distances, like a drive out of town. A fence, a bench and a window are just metres or centimetres.

questions.question: Sara writes a postcard about her hike. She and her dad walked on the mountain trail all morning. Which distance fits their hike best?
questions.explain: A whole morning of walking is kilometres. 6 metres is only about as long as a car, so it is far too short for a hike.

questions.question: Ella runs 300 metres, then 400 metres more. Liam runs 1 kilometre. How much farther did Liam run than Ella?
questions.explain: Ella ran 300 + 400 = 700 metres. Since 1 kilometre is 1000 metres (not 100), Liam ran 1000 - 700 = 300 metres more.

questions.question: Nina skates around the path at the rink. One loop is 300 metres long. She skates 3 loops. How far did she skate?
questions.explain: Three loops is 300 + 300 + 300 = 900 metres. That is not 9 kilometres, because every 1 kilometre takes a whole 1000 metres.

questions.question: Ryan writes this in his notebook: 1 kilometre = 100 metres. What went wrong?
options: He used 100, but 1 kilometre is 1000 metres
Nothing is wrong, 1 kilometre is 100 metres
He mixed it up, 1 metre is 1000 kilometres
He used 100, but 1 kilometre is 10 metres
questions.explain: 1 kilometre is 1000 metres, so Ryan should have written 1000. Many children write 100 here, because 1 metre is 100 centimetres.

questions.question: Ella walks 1 kilometre to school. Her school field is 100 metres long. About how many fields would fit along her walk?
questions.explain: 1 kilometre is 1000 metres, and ten 100-metre fields make 1000 metres. If you thought 1 kilometre was 100 metres, you would get only 1 field.
